title: What Is Go Used For? knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly covered in “What Is Go Used For?”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Go curriculum lists “Backend and web development” under “What Is Go Used For?”. The lesson uses that topic as the entry point for the example and practice task.

questions.prompt: Which result should you expect from the example for “What Is Go Used For?”, subject to the stated prerequisites?
options: Go is used for services, CLIs, networking, and infrastructure tools.
The program always prints an empty string.
The output is random on every run.
The code cannot produce an observable result.
questions.answer_key: Go is used for services, CLIs, networking, and infrastructure tools.
questions.explanation: Trace the example and its documented prerequisites. Expected result: Go is used for services, CLIs, networking, and infrastructure tools.. If the example is an inspection or integration pattern, the result is a description of the expected behavior rather than a claim that an external system was run.

questions.prompt: If your what is go used for? example behaves unexpectedly, what is the best next step?
options: Reduce the issue to a small reproducible case, check inputs and errors, then change one cause and retest.
Suppress all errors so the program appears to succeed.
Change several unrelated files at once and skip retesting.
Assume every runtime and dependency version behaves identically.
questions.answer_key: Reduce the issue to a small reproducible case, check inputs and errors, then change one cause and retest.
questions.explanation: A small reproducible case helps separate input mistakes, language semantics, toolchain differences, and external failures. Change one suspected cause and retest.

status_note: Answer keys and explanations must remain repository/backend-side and are returned only according to the existing knowledge-check submission flow.
